Class ListGridModel<T>

java.lang.Object
de.schladebeck.fx.grid.model.AbstractGridModel
de.schladebeck.fx.grid.model.ListGridModel<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the type of the items
All Implemented Interfaces:
GridModel
public class ListGridModel<T> extends AbstractGridModel

A model for a list of objects, one object per row and one column per getter.

ListGridModel<Person> people = new ListGridModel<Person>()
        .column("Name", Person::name)
        .column("Salary", Person::salary);
people.setAll(loadPeople());

Changes (setAll(Collection), add(Object), set(int, T), remove(int), ...) and the builders (column(String, Function), rowNames(Function)) may come from any thread. Changes from other threads are queued and applied on the JavaFX application thread in order, see AbstractGridModel.applyChange(Runnable). Reading methods (getItem(int), getItems(), ...) belong to the JavaFX application thread; a background thread keeps its own copy of what it needs.

To show an ObservableList that other code changes, use of(ObservableList): the grid then follows every change of it.

  • Method Details

    • of

      public static <T> ListGridModel<T> of(javafx.collections.ObservableList<T> list)

      A model showing list, which keeps the items: every change of the list reaches the grid without further calls, and the changing methods of the model, as well as editing in the grid, change the list.

      ObservableList<Person> people = FXCollections.observableArrayList(p -> new Observable[] {p.nameProperty()});
Grid grid = new Grid(ListGridModel.of(people).column("Name", Person::getName));
people.add(new Person("Ann"));          // inserts a row
people.getFirst().setName("Bea");       // repaints it, reported by the extractor
FXCollections.sort(people, byName);     // shows the new order
      • Added and removed items insert and delete rows, so the selection and the visible rows follow them as with add(Object) and remove(int). set updates a row; setAll and a new order (sort) change all rows.
      • Changes inside an item reach the grid if the list reports them: create it with an extractor, as above.
      • Like any list shown in a JavaFX control, change the list on the JavaFX application thread only, and call this method there or before the list is in use. The model's changing methods may still be called from any thread: they change the list on the JavaFX application thread, see AbstractGridModel.applyChange(Runnable).
      • The list holds the model weakly, so a list that lives on does not keep the model or its grid alive. The model follows the list for as long as something else holds it, such as the grid showing it.
      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the items
      Parameters:
      list - the items, one per row; modifiable if the model's changing methods or editing are used
      Returns:
      a model without columns; add them with column(String, Function)

    • removeRows

      public void removeRows(int... modelRows)
      Removes the items at the given model rows, e.g. people.removeRows(grid.getSelectedModelRows()). The rows may come in any order and more than once; they are taken as they are before the first one is removed. Fires one DELETE event per run of adjacent rows. Any thread.
      Parameters:
      modelRows - the rows to remove
      Throws:
      IndexOutOfBoundsException - if a row is out of range; nothing is removed then
